section: Racial groups of India - Risley and Guha classifications

Risley classification - racial types and regions

accepted.s: Which one of the following combinations correctly describes the Mongoloid racial type?
o: Long head, broad nose, dark complexion and wavy hair
Tall stature, fair complexion, long head and light eyes
Dark skin, woolly hair, short stature and broad flat nose
Yellowish complexion, oblique eyes with epicanthic fold, high cheekbones and sparse hair
accepted.x: The Mongoloid type is characterised by yellowish complexion, oblique eyes with an epicanthic fold, high cheekbones, sparse hair, medium height, broad head and a flat face.
accepted.tq: Match the distinctive physical traits with the racial type.
accepted.sec: Physical traits → racial type (complexion, eye shape, cheek bones, hair, stature)

accepted.s: The Negrito racial type is generally associated with which one of the following sets of traits?
o: Yellowish complexion, sparse hair and broad head
Dark skin, woolly or frizzy hair, short stature and broad flat nose
Fair complexion, light eyes and tall stature
Olive-brown skin, straight hair and high nasal bridge
accepted.x: The Negrito type is described by dark skin, woolly or frizzy hair, short stature and a broad flat nose.
accepted.tq: Use a direct physical-trait identification question.
accepted.sec: Physical traits → racial type (complexion, eye shape, cheek bones, hair, stature)

accepted.s:
With reference to racial types, consider the following statements:
1. Proto-Australoids are associated with dark skin, wavy hair and a long head.
2. Nordic people are generally tall, fair, long-headed and light-eyed.
3. Dravidians, in Risley's classification, are associated with a long head, broad nose and dark complexion.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements correctly describe the listed racial types. Proto-Australoids have dark skin and wavy hair; Nordic people are tall and fair; and Risley's Dravidian type has a long head, broad nose and dark complexion.
accepted.tq: Check each statement against the associated physical traits.
accepted.sec: Physical traits → racial type (complexion, eye shape, cheek bones, hair, stature)

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the cephalic index?
o: Maximum length divided by maximum breadth, multiplied by 100
Maximum breadth divided by maximum length, multiplied by 100
Stature divided by head length, multiplied by 100
Nasal breadth divided by nasal length, multiplied by 100
accepted.x: Cephalic index is calculated as (maximum breadth / maximum length) × 100.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact formula rather than the reversed ratio.
accepted.sec: Physical traits → racial type (complexion, eye shape, cheek bones, hair, stature)

accepted.s: S.S. Sarkar classified racial groups primarily on the basis of which one of the following?
accepted.x: S.S. Sarkar's classification was based on the cephalic index, which measures head shape.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the classifier from the index used by Risley.
accepted.sec: Physical traits → racial type (complexion, eye shape, cheek bones, hair, stature)

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly gives the cephalic-index ranges for a living dolichocephalic head and a dry dolichocephalic skull, respectively?
accepted.x: A living dolichocephalic head has a cephalic index of 76.99 or below, while a dry skull has a value of 74.99 or below.
accepted.tq: Separate living-head and dry-skull ranges before selecting the pair.
accepted.sec: Physical traits → racial type (complexion, eye shape, cheek bones, hair, stature)

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Mesocephalic living head — 77–81.99
2. Mesocephalic dry skull — 75–79.99
3. Brachycephalic living head — 82 and above
4. Brachycephalic dry skull — 80 and above
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: All four pairs are correct. The living-head ranges are 77–81.99 for mesocephalic and 82 or above for brachycephalic; the corresponding dry-skull ranges are 75–79.99 and 80 or above.
accepted.tq: Compare the living-head and dry-skull columns systematically.
accepted.sec: Physical traits → racial type (complexion, eye shape, cheek bones, hair, stature)

accepted.s: A person has a nasal index of 86. Under the stated classification, this person would belong to which nasal category?
accepted.x: Platyrrhine refers to a broad nose with a nasal index of 85 or above. Leptorrhine is below 70 and mesorrhine is 70–84.9.
accepted.tq: Apply the numerical boundary to the category instead of recalling labels alone.
accepted.sec: Physical traits → racial type (complexion, eye shape, cheek bones, hair, stature)

accepted.s: Who among the following relied on the nasal index in racial classification?
accepted.x: H.H. Risley relied on the nasal index. S.S. Sarkar used the cephalic index, while Topinard is associated here with stature classification.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between similarly associated anthropological scholars.
accepted.sec: Physical traits → racial type (complexion, eye shape, cheek bones, hair, stature)

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Leptorrhine denotes a narrow nose with an index under 70. A broad nose with an index of 85 or above is platyrrhine.
accepted.tq: Find the reversed definition in the nasal-index classification.
accepted.sec: Physical traits → racial type (complexion, eye shape, cheek bones, hair, stature)

accepted.s: According to Topinard's stature classification, which one of the following is correct?
o: Tall means 180 cm or more and small means under 170 cm
Tall means 170 cm or more and small means under 160 cm
Tall means 175 cm or more and small means under 165 cm
Tall means 160 cm or more and small means under 150 cm
accepted.x: Topinard classified a stature of 170 cm or more as tall and a stature under 160 cm as small.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact cut-off values and avoid shifting both limits upward.
accepted.sec: Physical traits → racial type (complexion, eye shape, cheek bones, hair, stature)

accepted.s: Which of the following statements is correct regarding modern scientific understanding of human races?
o: Human populations differ in more than half of their genetic material.
Genetic material is identical only within a racial group.
All humans share over 99% of their genetic material, and modern science rejects ranking by race.
Race-based ranking is scientifically accepted because genetic differences are decisive.
accepted.x: Modern science rejects ranking people by race; all humans share over 99% of their genetic material.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise scientific conclusion rather than an extreme generalisation.
accepted.sec: Physical traits → racial type (complexion, eye shape, cheek bones, hair, stature)

accepted.s: Which one of the following combinations is correctly matched in the Caucasoid, Mongoloid and Negroid comparison?
o: Caucasoid—high bridge and narrow nose; Mongoloid—low to medium bridge; Negroid—low bridge and broad nose
Caucasoid—woolly hair; Mongoloid—wavy hair; Negroid—straight coarse hair
Caucasoid—high B blood group; Mongoloid—both A and B; Negroid—more A than B
Caucasoid—vertical eye fold; Mongoloid—occasional lateral fold; Negroid—medial epicanthic fold
accepted.x: Caucasoids have a high nasal bridge and narrow nose, Mongoloids a low-to-medium bridge, and Negroids a low bridge and broad nose. The other options interchange hair, blood-group or eye features.
accepted.tq: Start with the distinctive nose comparison and eliminate swapped traits.
accepted.sec: Physical traits → racial type (complexion, eye shape, cheek bones, hair, stature)

accepted.s: Which racial group is associated with straight, coarse hair described as leiotrichi?
accepted.x: Straight, coarse hair, termed leiotrichi, is associated with the Mongoloid group. Woolly or frizzy hair, termed ulotrichi, is associated with the Negroid group.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the similar hair classifications by their exact technical terms.
accepted.sec: Physical traits → racial type (complexion, eye shape, cheek bones, hair, stature)

accepted.s: H.H. Risley was the Census Commissioner for which census and wrote which book?
o: Census of 1931; The Races of India
Census of 1901; The People of India
Census of 1881; The Tribes of India
accepted.x: H.H. Risley was the Census Commissioner for 1901 and wrote The People of India, published in 1908.
accepted.tq: Link the official position, census year and book title in one recall unit.
accepted.sec: Risley classification - racial types and regions

accepted.s: The book The People of India by H.H. Risley was published in:
accepted.x: H.H. Risley's The People of India was published in 1908.
accepted.tq: Separate the census year from the publication year.
accepted.sec: Risley classification - racial types and regions

accepted.s: H.H. Risley is particularly associated with which one of the following ideas?
accepted.x: Risley was the exponent of the racial theory of caste, which treats caste as a by-product of racial difference.
accepted.tq: Identify the scholar by his characteristic theory.
accepted.sec: Risley classification - racial types and regions

accepted.s: Which one of the following Risley racial types is associated with Baluchistan and the North-West Frontier Province?
accepted.x: The Turko-Iranian type was associated with Baluchistan and the North-West Frontier region.
accepted.tq: Match the regional distribution with the correct Risley type.
accepted.sec: Risley classification - racial types and regions

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Indo-Aryan — Punjab, Rajasthan and Kashmir
2. Scytho-Dravidian — Maharashtra, Saurashtra and Coorg
3. Aryo-Dravidian — Uttar Pradesh and Bihar
4. Mongolo-Dravidian — Bengal and Odisha
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: All four pairs are correctly matched in Risley's regional classification.
accepted.tq: Verify each region independently before choosing the coded combination.
accepted.sec: Risley classification - racial types and regions

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched under Risley's classification?
o: Dravidian — South India, Chota Nagpur and central India
accepted.x: Punjab, Rajasthan and Kashmir were associated with the Indo-Aryan type. Scytho-Dravidian was associated with western India, including Maharashtra, Saurashtra and Coorg.
accepted.tq: Use the region swap trap to identify the incorrectly matched pair.
accepted.sec: Risley classification - racial types and regions

accepted.s: Paniyans and Santals are cited as examples of which Risley racial type?
accepted.x: Paniyans and Santals are cited as representative examples of the Dravidian type in Risley's classification.
accepted.tq: Recall representative populations rather than relying only on regional clues.
accepted.sec: Risley classification - racial types and regions

accepted.s: B.S. Guha's classification of the Indian population was based on which census data?
accepted.x: B.S. Guha used data from the 1931 Census for his classification of the Indian population.
accepted.tq: Distinguish Guha's census base from Risley's 1901 association.
accepted.sec: B.S. Guha classification - racial groups and representative populations

accepted.s: B.S. Guha classified Indians into:
accepted.x: Guha identified six main racial groups with nine sub-types, using 1931 Census data.
accepted.tq: Recall the paired count of main groups and sub-types.
accepted.sec: B.S. Guha classification - racial groups and representative populations

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched under B.S. Guha's classification?
o: Western Brachycephals — Alpinoid, Dinaric and Armenoid
Proto-Australoid — Munda, Santhal, Oraon, Bhil and Chenchu
accepted.x: Kadar and Irula are associated with the Negrito group. The Nordic group was associated with the north-west frontier and Punjab.
accepted.tq: Identify the representative population assigned to the wrong racial group.
accepted.sec: B.S. Guha classification - racial groups and representative populations

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements regarding Guha's Mongoloid group are correct?
1. It was divided into Palaeo-Mongoloid and Tibeto-Mongoloid.
2. Palaeo-Mongoloid included long-headed and broad-headed forms.
3. Tibeto-Mongoloid was associated with Sikkim and Bhutan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Guha divided the Mongoloid group into Palaeo-Mongoloid and Tibeto-Mongoloid. Palaeo-Mongoloid included long- and broad-headed forms, while Tibeto-Mongoloid was associated with Sikkim and Bhutan.
accepted.tq: Test the internal division, physical description and regional association together.
accepted.sec: B.S. Guha classification - racial groups and representative populations

accepted.s: Palaeo-Mediterranean, Mediterranean and Oriental are sub-types of which one of Guha's racial groups?
accepted.x: The Mediterranean group was divided into Palaeo-Mediterranean, Mediterranean and Oriental. The Oriental sub-type was associated with Punjab and Rajasthan.
accepted.tq: Match the sub-type cluster with its parent group.
accepted.sec: B.S. Guha classification - racial groups and representative populations

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
accepted.x: The Oriental sub-type of Guha's Mediterranean group was associated with Punjab and Rajasthan. Sema Nagas and Lepchas are examples of Palaeo-Mongoloid, while Parsis are associated with Armenoid.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure regional pair and reject representatives belonging to other sub-types.
accepted.sec: B.S. Guha classification - racial groups and representative populations

accepted.s: The Western Brachycephals in B.S. Guha's classification included which of the following sub-types?
accepted.x: Western Brachycephals comprised the Alpinoid, Dinaric and Armenoid sub-types. Parsis were cited as representatives of the Armenoid type.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the three sub-type groups by their exact composition.
accepted.sec: B.S. Guha classification - racial groups and representative populations

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly identifies the representative populations of the Palaeo-Mongoloid and Tibeto-Mongoloid sub-types, respectively?
o: Sema Nagas and Lepchas; Tibetans of Sikkim
Kadars and Irulas; Santhals and Bhils
accepted.x: Sema Nagas and Lepchas are examples of Palaeo-Mongoloid, while Tibetans of Sikkim represent Tibeto-Mongoloid. The latter are described as having a massive head, tall stature and light-brown skin.
accepted.tq: Use representative populations to discriminate between the two Mongoloid sub-types.
accepted.sec: B.S. Guha classification - racial groups and representative populations

accepted.s: Which one of the following combinations is correctly matched with the Negrito and Proto-Australoid groups in Guha's classification?
o: Negrito—Kadars and Irulas; Proto-Australoid—Santhals, Bhils and Chenchus
Negrito—Munda and Oraon; Proto-Australoid—Kadars and Irulas
accepted.x: Kadars and Irulas are associated with the Negrito group, while Santhals, Bhils and Chenchus are associated with the Proto-Australoid group.
accepted.tq: Pair each group with its representative populations before checking the options.
accepted.sec: B.S. Guha classification - racial groups and representative populations

accepted.s:
Arrange the following groups in the order in which they appear in B.S. Guha's six-group classification:
A. Mediterranean
B. Negrito
C. Nordic
D. Proto-Australoid
accepted.x: Guha's listed order is Negrito, Proto-Australoid, Mongoloid, Mediterranean, Western Brachycephals and Nordic. Therefore, among the groups given, the order is Negrito, Proto-Australoid, Mediterranean and Nordic.
accepted.tq: Use the stated sequence of the six groups and retain the relative order of the listed items.
accepted.sec: B.S. Guha classification - racial groups and representative populations

accepted.s: Which statement best describes the status of B.S. Guha's classification?
o: It was based exclusively on blood groups and not on census data.
It is the least cited classification of the Indian population.
It applies only to the populations of north-eastern India.
It is the most widely cited classification of the Indian population.
accepted.x: B.S. Guha's classification is the most widely cited classification of the Indian population and was based on 1931 Census data.
accepted.tq: Identify the evaluative conclusion associated with the classification.
accepted.sec: B.S. Guha classification - racial groups and representative populations
